### Was the table sent down?

Scholars differ over whether it came down, and the majority hold that it did. The apparent wording of the verse also states it, since Allah says He will send it down.

These reports testify that the table was sent down to the Children of Israel during the time of 'Isa as a result of Allah accepting his supplication. It is also among the favours Allah granted His servant and messenger 'Isa, accepting his request and sending it as clear proof and unequivocal evidence.

Ibn Abi Hatim records Ibn 'Abbas saying that they asked 'Isa to supplicate for a table spread with food from heaven, and that the angels brought the table down containing seven fish and seven pieces of bread and placed it before them, so that the last group ate as the first group did.

Ibn Jarir records Ishaq bin 'Abdullah saying that the table came down to 'Isa with seven pieces of bread and seven fish, and that they ate from it as much as they wished. When some of them stole food from it, saying that it might not come down tomorrow, the table ascended.

Another account relates that the angels descended with it from heaven, that on it were seven loaves and seven large fish, and that they ate until they were full. A hadith says the table consisted of bread and meat, and that they were commanded not to be treacherous and not to store anything for the next day, but they were treacherous and stored some of it, and were consequently transformed into apes and swine.

A report from 'Ammar ibn Yasir in At-Tirmidhi says the table came down from heaven with bread and meat, and that some of those people committed a breach of trust and kept it over for the next day, with the result that they were transformed into monkeys and swines. They ate from it as they wished, but storing it for later use was prohibited.

One gloss describes the punishment as turning them into swine, and adds that after eating they said this was clear magic. 'Isa is then reported as answering, O Allah, if You punish them for what they say they are Your servants, and if You forgive them, You are mighty in retribution toward whoever does not repent.

### Why is the punishment so severe?

Where Allah's blessing is extraordinary and unique, the emphasis on gratitude for it must be far above the ordinary, and the punishment for ingratitude will likewise be extraordinary and unique. That is what the verse teaches.

The reason lies in the removal of the veil. Crops flourishing in the fields, or a tree coming up stout and green from beneath the earth, are as much miraculous events as the descent of a platter of food from the clouds. Their miraculous nature is not apparent to us because they appear from behind a veil.

The test of a person is that he should be able to see the reality by tearing down that veil, and to look on the basic elements of food emerging from the earth as though they were descending from heaven. Whoever insists that he will accept divine truth only on seeing it is saying, in effect, that he will receive Allah's grace without undergoing His trial, and by Allah's way that is not possible.

Disbelief after a sign of this kind is therefore not one error among others. It is a refusal made with the veil removed, which is why the punishment attached to it has no parallel.

### In short

- Allah grants the request and warns that disbelief afterward will bring a punishment inflicted on no other creature.
- The three groups named for the severest torment are the hypocrites, the disbelievers among the people of the table and the people of Fir'awn.
- The majority hold that the table was sent down, with reports describing seven loaves and seven fish, eating until satisfied, and ascent after some stole or stored from it.
- A hadith describes the treacherous being transformed into apes and swine, and storing for the next day as prohibited.
- Ordinary provision is miraculous behind a veil, and demanding the veil be lifted removes the condition of trial, which explains the severity of the warning.
